items.title: Paul Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: And the only thing that could have prevented that would have been Jobim with the bossa nova, but the bossa nova was too hard.

ctx.x: It’s still the blues. Curious you say that because we’ve in the past years, it’s being elevated to a real art form, in the universities and with Jazz at Lincoln Center and all that.

Well it’s like jazz basically, if you really get down to the nitty gritty of the thing, it’s nothing more than creating a new melody out of your head on a basic set of chords, either from another tune or chords that you write yourself. But that’s it. There’s no great story with it, I don’t think. I mean I’ve never been able to — you know the guys that really took it seriously and really didn’t work to an audience, killed it for a long time there, especially the bop era. I blame the bop era for the advent of rock,…
But the youth wanted their own music and since it wasn’t being offered to them—
